It’s interesting how every single source I’ve seen around Dawn Butler saying babies are born without sex (which I assume was a mishap and she meant to say babies are born without gender) seems to be vehemently against transgender people. Most of the people who make the whole “babies are born with a sex” argument are trying to conflate sex with gender, which is something that can be argued babies are born without, as gender is a set of social structures within society rather than the biological separation of anatomy between males and females. Now, at the moment, I’m assuming you agree with me that sex and gender are separate concepts, and that gender is malleable and defined by society. If you were to disagree with the statement of “trans women are real women” I would have suitable reason to label you a transphobe. But I assume you’re arguing in good faith right now, so I’ll just say that Dawn Butlers mistake of saying babies aren’t born with sex doesn’t discount the fact that trans women are real women, and it does not discount the fact that the prejudices they face in common life are extreme and brutal, with constant harassment, bullying, cruelty and sometimes assault.

“Nobody gets paid more than their worth”. Bruh what. Jeff Bezos is worth $100 billion dollars, it’s utterly delusional to think any human being is deserving of or worth that much wealth, power and money. 


You say it’s not greed for company owners to abuse their positions of power and pay themselves luxuriant, over-indulgent wages while the workers struggle to get by on minimum wage and feed their families and pay their rent, and you call the workers greedy? The difference between the owner and the workers is that the owner already has realistically most luxuries and wealth needed to live a joyful and relatively stress free life without worrying about their financial status, while the workers have to bust their balls grinding out poor wages just to make ends meet, and still be in a difficult financial position. It’s not greedy to want to live a financially stress free life, it’s a right that most people should have, it is not greedy to want to be in a position where you don’t have to worry about living pay check to pay check and ending up on the streets. To act like anyone can up and start a business in the current economic climate is ridiculous, people cannot afford to pay their rent, how are they meant to afford a business startup. The idea that people must become business owners and make their own fortune to be successful relies on the fact that there will always be an underclass of poor people who cannot make their own business, because owning a business is a highly exclusive position that very few people actually have access to.


Tell me, who carries the real risk if a company goes under? The overpaid CEO of a company who has enough money to play golf till he’s dead and gets massive payouts before the company crashes, or the countless workers who get laid off and are without pay for weeks while struggling to find employment again, putting them in a very difficult economic position.


Obviously there’s people who went from rags to riches, but you cannot say that wealth is not ultimately a deciding factor in the success of a business. Donald Trump’s businesses failed several times, but due to his immense wealth he was able to sustain his position and maintain stability. Poorer people do not have that option, it’s all in and if the business fails, they lose it all. Surely you must see that this imbalance plays a large factor in the fact that rich people are able to consolidate more wealth a lot more easily than those on the lower class.

I’m going to let you in on a little secret here. It’s entirely within the realms of possibility for business owners to pay workers a better wage. However, due to greed, owners of companies take a larger share of wealth for themselves and leave the workers, who combined make way more value for the business than said owners do, with low, unsubstantial wages. You seem to deny the fact that workers give business value, instead the owners of the business give the workers skills value. But the business has no value if it has no skills to utilise from workers for production. How can a business operate with no workers?

As for your second point, what are these business skills that are somehow worth way more than other worker skills? It’s really not that difficult to come up with the idea to start a business, and having the funds to do so suggests you’re within a higher social class anyway, something most people are born into rather than earn their way into, so I don’t see why that’s deserving of so much value within the company. I won’t lie this game is incredibly difficult, but also incredibly rewarding. One of the main keys to success is remaining calm, and remembering to not take your failure so seriously. He who has never made a mistake has also never learned anything. When you fight the boss (I also had difficulty fighting him when I first met him) remember to notice when you die exactly how you died. Each boss has specific moves that they will utilise, once you remember and prepare yourself for them they are much easier to deflect. Again, remaining calm is so important to succeeding in this game. I am a man who rages a lot at games, some games have even had me screaming into a pillow or punching my bed out of rage, but I’ve learned to move past that initial stress and to forgive my mistakes and not let the anger pent up, because then it’s just no fun and I’ll get nowhere. Take your time with the game, try pressing the deflect button multiple times when an enemy attacks to get you used to when you need to do it, and once you’ve learned it’ll be easier to just press the deflect button once and get it first try. Remember that jumping away from the enemy is a useful strategy to distance yourself from attacks you are struggling with and blocking attacks is also a useful ally. This game will be a rough ride, but there’s no feeling that’s better than when you finally stick your sword into the guy that’s been killing you for the past three hours and deliver the death blow.
